pages.title: Welcome to Arcwright
pages.body: A game engine built for AI. Your AI app, or Arcwright's built-in AI, builds in this editor while you watch every step. You can stop it, change it, or undo it at any time.

images.caption: A ship's passageway, forged by an AI in this editor

pages.title: What's new, and where to find it
pages.body: Everything below is in the editor you just opened. Your AI app can do each of these for you too: just ask.

steps.title: Your player moves like a real person
steps.detail: Select your player, then Inspector › Motion AI › Turn on Motion AI, and tick carries in its motion_ai component. Natural starts, stops and turns, feet planted. Or ask your AI: "let Motion AI carry my player".

steps.title: Web export
steps.detail: File › Export Game › Web (browser and phones) makes a folder you can put on any website: 2D and 3D games, packed small. It runs Arcwright's web packer, which needs Python 3 (the export tells you how to install it if it's missing).

steps.title: New faces and people
steps.detail: The human kit now ships inside Arcwright. Ask your AI for a person ("a 40-year-old pilot, short grey hair"): the Face Forger makes a brand-new face, and clothes are fitted to the body.

steps.title: Teach a character a walk from one video
steps.detail: Inspector › Motion AI › Make a style from a video…: a side-on clip of one person walking, whole body in view, still camera. A heavy brute, anyone.

steps.title: Exports are checked before they ship
steps.detail: File › Export Game checks every file it would ship. Anything too big for its platform is named, with the exact fix, so your game stays small.

steps.title: 24 military props to forge
steps.detail: Open a sample, then Assets › Forge › Military: ammo cans, crates, cots, a stretcher, a radio, sandbag walls, work lamps and more. Ask your AI to forge one ("forge Military/ammo_can") and change the recipe to make it yours.

steps.title: Smooth starts and steady frame rates
steps.detail: Exported games no longer freeze on first launch. Ask your AI to set your game's target frame rate (60 for a fast game); it holds a steady 30 when a computer can't keep up.

steps.title: Royalty-free to $1 million
steps.detail: Your game is royalty-free until it earns $1 million, then 5% of the revenue above that. Games made with earlier versions keep their old terms.

images.caption: The 24 military props, each built by the Forge from a recipe

pages.title: Everything happens on screen
pages.body: Follow AI keeps the camera on the work, and a caption says what the AI is doing. Drag the view and you're in control; Follow AI stays off until you turn it back on. Every change lands in History, where you can undo it.

images.caption: An AI placing a ready room's chairs, row by row

pages.title: From a picture to a real 3D model
pages.body: The AI writes a recipe (the shapes, sizes and materials) and the Forge builds it in stages you can watch: block out, add parts, round the edges, paint, then age it. Recipes are plain code in the Workshop panel, so you can read and edit them too.

pages.title: Give it a reference picture
pages.body: A good picture is the biggest quality boost you can give. The AI matches its shapes, colours and wear.
tips: A clear picture of the object on a plain background
Front and side views if you can
Say its real size: "a chair, 1 m tall"
For a room or a place, an eye-level photo

pages.eyebrow: People (new in Beta 3: the human kit ships)
pages.title: New faces with the Face Forger
pages.body: Describe a person (age, build, hair) and the Face Forger makes a brand-new face by blending a library of reference people, then adds age and weight. Clothes are then tailored to the body in the same editor.

images.caption: A commanding officer, briefing his squadron

pages.title: Motion AI: walks, runs and your player, made live
pages.body: A motion AI (NVIDIA MotionBricks) makes a 3D character's walk, jog and run step by step as it moves, instead of replaying the same clips. New in Beta 3: it can drive the character you control, with natural starts, stops and turns. Sprints still use the clips for now.

steps.title: Turn it on
steps.detail: Select a 3D character and press Turn on Motion AI in the Inspector's Motion AI section. Press Play and walk or run.

steps.title: Let it carry your player
steps.detail: On your player, also tick carries in its motion_ai component (Inspector): the motion AI then moves the body itself, so the feet stay planted.

steps.title: Tune the walk
steps.detail: Live in Play: presets relaxed / brisk / heavy, plus lean, hip height (lower), stride, arm swing, step width, speed range.

steps.title: Teach it a new walk
steps.detail: Make a style from a video… learns from a side-on video of one person walking, whole body in view, still camera.

steps.title: Or ask your AI
steps.detail: "Make this character walk naturally" does the same.

pages.title: What's strong today, and what we're improving
pages.body: Arcwright is in Beta. We'd rather you know the edges up front. Every update moves something from the right column to the left.

columns.title: Strong today
items: Rooms, buildings and interiors with real detail
Cinematics: cameras, voices, lip sync, music
Motion AI: walks, runs and your own player made live
Exports checked before they ship: small, complete games

columns.title: Still improving
items: Clothes fitting people; arms and legs passing through things
Animation: sprints and very sharp turns with Motion AI, sitting, standing up
Whole games from one sentence: build them step by step with your AI instead

pages.title: Your reports make it better
pages.body: We fix what people tell us about. The most useful reports show the gap between what you wanted and what you got.

steps.title: Send feedback
steps.detail: Help › Send Feedback. Say what you asked for and what came out. You can attach a picture of the Arcwright window.

steps.title: Show what you wanted
steps.detail: Include your reference picture, or name the real object. "It should look like this" is gold.

steps.title: Let crash reports through
steps.detail: If Arcwright closes unexpectedly, it asks once whether to send a report. You see everything in it first; your name and home folder are removed.

steps.title: Ask your AI to write it up
steps.detail: Your AI knows which tool it used and what went wrong. Ask it for a short summary and paste it into your feedback.

pages.title: Start building
pages.body: Connect the AI app you already use, or take a two-minute tour of the editor first.
